# dtcloud_image (Resource)

Manages a disk image and the file behind it.

Creating one is two requests and a wait: the first opens an empty record, the second uploads the file, and the image is usable only once it reaches `active`. Both happen during apply, because an image with no data is a record no machine can boot from.

`name`, `os_distro`, `min_disk` and `visibility` change in place. Everything else forces replacement, including the file: no endpoint replaces the data of an existing image.

`protected` is deliberately not exposed. The API accepts it at create time but cannot clear it afterwards, which would make the image impossible to destroy through this provider.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_image" "golden" {
  name        = "golden-ubuntu-22.04"
  source_file = "${path.module}/images/ubuntu-22.04.qcow2"
  disk_format = "qcow2"
  os_distro   = "ubuntu"
  min_disk    = 20

  min_ram    = 2048
  visibility = "private"
  uefi       = false
  tags       = ["golden", "ubuntu"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `disk_format` (String) Format of the file, such as `qcow2` or `iso`. The accepted values come from the platform's own configuration rather than from a list in the provider, so an unsupported one is refused by the API during apply. Not the same thing as the `type` attribute, which is a display category derived from it.
- `min_disk` (Number) Smallest volume, in GB, a machine built from this image needs. Can be changed in place. The API reports it as the text `20 GB`, which the provider parses back into a number.
- `name` (String) Name of the image. Can be changed in place. Names are not unique on the platform, which is why `dtcloud_image` prefers a lookup by id.
- `os_distro` (String) Distribution the image carries, such as `ubuntu`. Like `disk_format`, the accepted values are the platform's and are checked by the API. Can be changed in place.
- `source_file` (String) Path to the local disk file to upload. The file is read during apply and must still be there. There is no endpoint that replaces the data of an existing image, so changing this builds a new one.

### Optional

- `min_ram` (Number) Smallest amount of RAM, in MB, a machine built from this image needs. Write-only: no endpoint reports it back, so it cannot drift and does not survive an import.
- `source_file_hash` (String) Hash of the file, used to notice that its contents changed while its path did not — set it to `filesha256(var.path)` or similar. Nothing reads the file during plan, so without this a modified file goes unnoticed.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags to attach to the image. Write-only, like `min_ram`: accepted on create and reported by nothing.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `uefi` (Boolean) Boot the image with UEFI firmware instead of BIOS. Unlike the other create-only arguments this one is reported back, so a change made elsewhere shows up as drift.
- `visibility` (String) Who can see the image: `public`, `private`, `shared` or `community`. Defaults to `shared`, which is what the API applies when the field is omitted. Can be changed in place.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `os_type` (String) `linux` or `windows`, when the platform reports it. Frequently empty here: the details endpoint passes the value straight through, while the list endpoint behind `dtcloud_images` guesses it from `os_distro` when it is missing.
- `size` (String) Size of the uploaded data, as the platform formats it — `1.5 GB` or `250 MB`. There is no endpoint that reports it as a number. An image with no data yet reads as `0 MB`.
- `status` (String) Status reported by the platform. `active` is the only status a machine can be built from; `queued` and `saving` mean the data is not there yet, and `killed` means the upload failed.
- `type` (String) How the platform categorises the image: `ISO` or `Template (VM)`. This is not `disk_format` — it is derived from it, and the two are not interchangeable.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# The file behind an image cannot be read back, so source_file and
# source_file_hash stay at whatever the configuration says after an import.
terraform import dtcloud_image.golden 1f6b8d24-3e70-49ca-8d15-4b2f7a9c6e77
```
